flashcards.q: How is chapter used in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: This chapter teaches you how to write the instructions that make AI produce reliable, accurate and on-brand work for sales, marketing and customer success, and how to turn good prompts into shared team assets that are versioned, tested and improved like any other part of the revenue system.

flashcards.q: How should wording not be handled in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Choose examples that share the qualities you want (length, structure, tone) but differ in surface wording. - **Match the task.** An example of a cold outreach email does not teach the model how to write a renewal reminder.

flashcards.q: What does Prompt Design For Revenue Teams teach about per-request input?
flashcards.a: Explain what a prompt is, the difference between standing instructions and per-request input, and why prompt wording changes output so much.

flashcards.q: What should be avoided with want in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: A language model has no fixed understanding of what you want.

flashcards.q: When is per-request input applied in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: A representative writes per-request input when asking an assistant for help; a sales operations lead or enablement manager writes the standing instructions that every representative's requests pass through.

flashcards.q: When should prompts not be used in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: First, prompts must be written carefully and specifically, not dashed off.

flashcards.q: Where does king Academy come up in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: The chapter closes with a field case from the Sales King Academy platform, where an irrelevant record in the context took over answers across agents until a relevance gate was added, and a lab in which you design and score instructions for an agent of your own.

flashcards.q: Is source badge always required in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Each chat reply carries a source badge showing whether it came from deterministic recall, verified knowledge, the web or AI generation.

flashcards.q: Is pressure tactics ever unnecessary in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Constraints: no invented proof points, no disparaging competitors, no pressure tactics such as false urgency, and no concessions on price or terms.

flashcards.q: Which approach to token fits Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Select and budget context for a prompt, estimating its token count and running cost at volume.

flashcards.q: Who is involved with chapter in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: This chapter teaches you how to write the instructions that make AI produce reliable, accurate and on-brand work for sales, marketing and customer success, and how to turn good prompts into shared team assets that are versioned, tested and improved like any other part of the revenue system.

flashcards.q: Who should not be handling knack in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Prompt design is therefore a team discipline, not an individual knack.

flashcards.q: Why does honest matter in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: The purpose is a relevant, honest first message to someone who has a reason to hear from you.

flashcards.q: How is approved claims used in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: A proposal might be drafted in three steps: extract the buyer's goals from discovery notes into a structured list; draft the situation section from that list; check the draft against the list and the approved claims.

flashcards.q: What does Prompt Design For Revenue Teams teach about usually assembled?
flashcards.a: In business systems, it is usually assembled from several pieces: standing instructions written once by the team, data pulled from the CRM or a document, the specific request, and sometimes examples of good output.

flashcards.q: What should be avoided with knack in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Prompt design is therefore a team discipline, not an individual knack.

flashcards.q: When is prompts applied in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Second, the same prompt can behave differently on a different model, or after a provider updates a model, so prompts must be retested when models change.

flashcards.q: When should call notes not be used in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Context.** The information the model needs and could not know otherwise: the call notes, the buyer's role, the products discussed, the agreed next step, relevant approved claims.

flashcards.q: Where does chapter come up in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Relevance of context matters as much as its accuracy, a lesson the field case in this chapter shows directly.

flashcards.q: Is same answer always required in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Also record from steps 1 and 2: whether numbers matched across modes, whether the repeated question gave the same answer, and which badge the live question received.

flashcards.q: Is fake ever unnecessary in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: That rules out invented testimonials and reviews, fabricated customer results, fake scarcity ("only two places left" when that is not true), false claims of a personal relationship, and messages that pretend to be personally written by someone who never saw them.

flashcards.q: Which approach to covered fits Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Only the bracketed parts change per call, which makes it a natural candidate for a template, covered in Section 6.

flashcards.q: Who is involved with reusable prompt in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Build reusable prompt templates and manage a team prompt library with owners, versions and change records.

flashcards.q: Who should not be handling call notes in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Context.** The information the model needs and could not know otherwise: the call notes, the buyer's role, the products discussed, the agreed next step, relevant approved claims.

flashcards.q: Why does king Academy matter in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: The Sales King Academy chat shows a source badge on each reply for this reason, and you will use it in the lab.

flashcards.q: How is easier used in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Chaining makes each step simpler and easier to test, and lets you use different settings, or different models, for different steps.

flashcards.q: What does Prompt Design For Revenue Teams teach about very?
flashcards.a: It infers it from the text it is given, and it is very sensitive to that text.

flashcards.q: What should be avoided with weak in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Not every prompt needs all six, but checking for each is a reliable way to improve a weak one.

flashcards.q: When is follow-up email applied in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: "Write a follow-up email to the buyer after a discovery call." One task per prompt usually works better than several; a prompt that asks for an email, a CRM summary and a list of objections in one go tends to do all three less well than three separate prompts.

flashcards.q: When should game-changing not be used in Prompt Design For Revenue Teams?
flashcards.a: Never use 'synergy', 'revolutionary' or 'game-changing'." - **Reading level.** "Write so a busy manager can read it in 30 seconds; short sentences; no jargon unless the buyer used it first." - **Formatting.** "No more than three short paragraphs.
